title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: source context based file protection
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned source-based protection from existing Endpoint DLP controls. The documented policy-scoping path, PowerShell command and licensing match Microsoft guidance; independent searches found no published configuration or default for the new capability.

claims.claim: Existing Endpoint DLP conditions can describe file content.
claims.quote: Conditions supported for Endpoints: Content contains: Specifies content to be detected.

claims.claim: Existing Endpoint DLP includes controls concerned with where sensitive files are going.
claims.quote: Upload to a restricted cloud service domain or access from an unallowed browser: Detects when a user attempts to upload an item to a restricted service domain or access an item through a browser.

claims.claim: The sensitive-website condition concerns a website the user accesses in Microsoft Edge, rather than the provenance of a downloaded file.
claims.quote: We want to detect when users access these sensitive sites in supported browsers: Condition: User accessed a sensitive site from Edge.

Read dlp-policy-reference Endpoint conditions, dlp-configure-endpoint-settings, Set-DlpComplianceRule and Set-DlpCompliancePolicy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified whether source matches lead to auditing, blocking, labelling or encryption.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview source context Endpoint operating systems roles rollout audit block; opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about and dlp-policy-reference. Roadmap says only Protect file; existing action documentation does not describe this capability.

claims.claim: The roadmap and Microsoft Learn describe no identity change for this source-context capability.

claims.quote: Searched: Purview source context Endpoint operating systems roles rollout audit block; read roadmap description, endpoint-dlp-getting-started and dlp-create-deploy-policy Permissions. No source-context permission change found.

claims.claim: Microsoft lists Compliance administrator, Compliance data administrator, Information Protection, Information Protection Admin and Security administrator as role groups for creating and deploying DLP policies.
claims.quote: The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of these role groups: Compliance administrator; Compliance data administrator; Information Protection; Information Protection Admin; Security administrator.

claims.claim: No additional permission specific to source-context protection is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview source context Endpoint operating systems roles rollout audit block; opened dlp-create-deploy-policy Permissions, endpoint-dlp-getting-started and Set-DlpCompliancePolicy. Published permissions concern existing DLP, not a new source-context permission.

claims.claim: No autonomous or agent behaviour is described for this capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview source context Endpoint operating systems roles rollout audit block; read roadmap description and opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about and dlp-policy-reference. No autonomous or agent mechanism for source-context protection found.

claims.claim: Existing Endpoint DLP policy targeting can combine users and devices.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; rendered controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal path reaches the all-users scope of the Devices location through policy creation, Enterprise applications & devices, the Custom policy template and Full directory.
claims.quote: Data loss prevention > policies. Select Create policy. Select Enterprise applications & devices. Select the Custom from the Categories then Custom policy template from Regulations. Accept the default Full directory under Admin units. Devices location. Edit. All users, groups, and adaptive scopes.

claims.where: controls[1].api; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-DlpCompliancePolicy -Identity <policy> -AddEndpointDlpLocation <users> modifies the included user accounts of an Endpoint DLP policy under the stated prerequisite.
claims.quote: The AddEndpointDLPLocation parameter specifies the user accounts to add to the list of included accounts for Endpoint DLP if you used the value All for the EndpointDLPLocation parameter. You identify the account by name or email address.

claims.where: controls[1].note; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: AddEndpointDlpLocation requires EndpointDLPLocation to have been set to All.
claims.quote: The AddEndpointDLPLocation parameter specifies the user accounts to add to the list of included accounts for Endpoint DLP if you used the value All for the EndpointDLPLocation parameter.

claims.where: controls[1].note; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: AddEndpointDlpLocation requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator membership in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Note: This parameter requires membership in the Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator roles in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: The documented alternative controls which users an existing Endpoint DLP policy covers in its Devices location.
claims.quote: When a DLP policy includes the Devices location, the policy can be scoped by both users and devices. For a DLP policy to be enforced on an endpoint, both the user and the device must be included in the policy scope.

claims.where: controls[1].note; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: The user-scoping control does not itself configure source-based file protection.
claims.quote: The AddEndpointDLPLocation parameter specifies the user accounts to add to the list of included accounts for Endpoint DLP if you used the value All for the EndpointDLPLocation parameter.
